name: Times club monthly special crossword No 20,182

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tree has sort of perch in black and gold

indicators.note: 'in' places the fish inside the pair of letters for gold

blocks.note: B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black
the bass is a fish of the perch family
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A tree with a fish perched among black and gold decorations.
explanation.walkthrough: The gold symbol is split by the fish, with black placed in front; 'perch' misleads as a roost, but here it is a fish family.
explanation.definitionFit: The babassu is a Brazilian palm whose nuts yield a valuable oil.

clue.text: Fish from seat ace watch

blocks.note: informal British word for the backside
A marks an ace on playing cards
lo is an old command meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone fishing from a seat, with a watch for timing.
explanation.definitionFit: The bummalo, or Bombay duck, is a small South Asian fish, usually dried and salted.

clue.text: Dealing informally with sound of snoring stifling a flamboyant vigour

indicators.note: to stifle something is to smother it, so the snoring letters close round the next item

blocks.note: biz is slang for business, that is commercial dealing
the cartoon sound of someone asleep
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone snoring through a showy business presentation.
explanation.walkthrough: The snore is the cartoon triple Z, opened after its first letter to take the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizzazz is a variant spelling of pizzazz, meaning showy energy and dash.

clue.text: Some scepticism as hero overcomes supreme being

indicators.note: 'Some' takes just part of the run of letters that follows

blocks.note: found running across the end of the first word, the next two, and the start of the last

explanation.surface: A sceptic's doubts give way when a heroic figure defeats a god.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'supreme being' sounds theological, but here it is something supremely good.
explanation.definitionFit: A smasheroo is slang for an outstanding success or something excellent, a thing that beats all others.

clue.text: Pulp stripped out of prickly shrub

indicators.note: something stripped has its outer covering removed, leaving only its core

blocks.note: the inside two letters of the word
ex is Latin for out of

explanation.surface: Clearing gorse by reducing its stems to pulp.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulex is the botanical genus of gorse or furze, a spiny yellow-flowered bush.

clue.text: You initially should wear pants, boy in Highlands argued

indicators.note: 'initially' asks for the opening letter of the word before it
to wear something is to have it on, so the trousers go round the single letter

blocks.note: first letter
pants and naff are both British slang for rubbish or worthless
a short boy's name, Edward

explanation.surface: A Scottish lad is told he must put his trousers on, and protests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' is not trousers here but British slang for rubbish, and the initial letter goes in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nyaff is a Scots verb meaning to yap or bicker, so its past tense means quarrelled pettily.

clue.text: Repeated invalid answer, getting stick Down Under

blocks.note: null and void means invalid
A is the standard abbreviation for answer
the two pieces written out a second time

explanation.surface: A quiz contestant keeps giving the same wrong answer and gets beaten in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeated' sits at the front of the clue but applies to the whole two-part piece that follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A nulla-nulla is a heavy hardwood club used by Aboriginal Australians, hence a stick in Australia.

clue.text: Rabbis very regularly giving the basics

indicators.note: 'regularly' means taking letters at even intervals, here every second one

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Rabbis teaching elementary principles to their students.
explanation.definitionFit: Absey is an archaic form of ABC, the alphabet, and so the first elements of any subject.

clue.text: Rug elevated floor area in lift fantastically

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised up means read from bottom to top
done fantastically means done in a wild, unreal way, so the letters are jumbled
'in' sets the earlier pieces inside the jumbled word

blocks.note: the letters of lift rearranged, split to take the insert
to floor someone is to knock them out, a KO
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Using a lift to carry a rug up to the top floor.
explanation.walkthrough: To floor someone is to knock them out; in a down clue 'elevated' reads that from the bottom up. 'lift' looks like the elevator but is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A flokati is a thick, shaggy Greek woollen rug, woven and then felted.

clue.text: Perjury by Ulster politicians coming back again in Caledonian court

definitions.text: coming back again in Caledonian court

blocks.note: the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland
perjury is lying under oath

explanation.surface: Northern Irish politicians accused of lying in a Scottish court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' puts the party next to the lying, and the party comes first. Ulster is Northern Ireland; Caledonian means Scottish.
explanation.definitionFit: In old Scots law a duply is a defender's second answer, so duplying is making that rejoinder in court.

clue.text: Roll amazes, prepared with unknown cheeses

indicators.note: something prepared has been made up or worked into shape, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: the letters taken as written
x, y and z are the unknowns in algebra

explanation.surface: A bread roll is amazingly good when filled with an unidentified cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozzarella is a soft white Italian cheese, traditionally from buffalo milk; the plural fits 'cheeses'.

clue.text: Scottish join in brief admission of carelessness

indicators.note: something brief is cut short, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: what you say on making a careless slip

explanation.surface: A Scottish joiner briefly owns up to a slapdash mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: OOPS loses its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Oop is a Scots verb meaning to bind or tie together, so to unite things.

clue.text: Church close to rectory on field subject to drainage

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is wanted

blocks.note: a lea is a meadow, a poetic word for a field
CH is the abbreviation for church
last letter

explanation.surface: A church and rectory standing by a waterlogged field.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'on' puts the church pieces after the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Leachy means porous, letting water percolate through, so liable to have soluble matter washed out.

clue.text: Old reservists see inside method — and also vote against

indicators.note: 'inside' sets the letter for see within the word for method, and the same again with the vote

blocks.note: a way of doing something is a method
v is short for vide, Latin for see
a no vote
the letter for see is used a second time

explanation.surface: Veteran reservists consider a proposal and vote it down.
explanation.walkthrough: The one 'see' does duty twice. The officers' wavy gold sleeve stripes gave the force its nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wavy Navy was the nickname of the old Royal Naval Volunteer Reserve, a body of part-time sailors.

clue.text: Dodgy lymphatics possessed by grasping person?

indicators.note: dodgy means unsound or unreliable, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A suspect lymph system belonging to someone in a doctor's grip.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition describes rather than names: what a greedy person is said to have.
explanation.definitionFit: To have an itchy palm is an idiom for being greedy for money, the mark of an avaricious person.

clue.text: Girl so represented in art of Eastern religion

indicators.note: to represent is to present again in another form, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: a girl's name
so and thus both mean in this way
the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl portrayed in a work of art from an Asian faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Zarathustrian relates to Zarathustra, or Zoroaster, founder of the ancient Persian faith Zoroastrianism.

clue.text: A rock or two held by pin, note

indicators.note: something held by another is gripped within it, so the numeral sits inside

blocks.note: a thole is a peg or pin on a boat's gunwale serving as a rowlock
Roman numeral
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A climber's rock pitch protected by a couple of pins.
explanation.walkthrough: The numeral is held between the two parts that follow it, the pin and the note.
explanation.definitionFit: Tholeiite is a type of basalt, a dark volcanic stone poor in alkalis.

clue.text: Preserve following regulation old public transport to convey a judge

indicators.note: to convey is to carry, so the vehicle carries the next letters inside it

blocks.note: ex- means former
a tram is a street-running passenger vehicle
taken as written
J is the abbreviation for judge

explanation.surface: An old tram carrying a judge, with a jar of preserves on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preserve' looks like a verb, but it is the noun, and the definition runs on to the rules it obeys.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra jam is a legally defined grade of jam with a higher fruit content, as set by food regulations.

clue.text: Recalled stain covering old hospital photos capturing plant with sword-shaped leaves

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the stated string is read backwards
covering means wrapping round, so the stain goes around the next item
capturing means seizing and holding inside, so the reversed string takes in the final item

blocks.note: to sully is to soil or stain
O is the abbreviation for old
H is the map sign for hospital
informal plural of picture
the hop is a climbing plant used in brewing

explanation.surface: Old hospital photographs, discoloured by a stain, show a plant with spiky leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal covers everything from 'stain' to 'photos'; only after that does the result capture the plant. 'plant' belongs to the wordplay, so the definition is the adjectival phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: From Greek xiphos, sword, and phyllon, leaf: the term describes foliage like that of an iris.

clue.text: Stroke, but not repeatedly, having arms expanding out

blocks.note: to pat is to stroke gently
done a single time only

explanation.surface: Stroking someone just the one time, arms flung wide.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a cross patonce has limbs that widen toward the ends, finishing in flared points.

clue.text: When climbing, stick protection on foot

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means read upwards, from bottom to top

blocks.note: as and when both mean at the time that
a baton is a short stick

explanation.surface: Advice to a mountaineer to carry a walking stick and wear protective boots.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabaton is the jointed steel shoe of a suit of armour, guarding a knight's feet.

clue.text: Cut out and tick uninitiated message boxes

indicators.note: someone uninitiated has not been let in at the start, so the word loses its first letter
to box is to enclose, so the shortened word goes round the other piece

blocks.note: a text is a phone message
a tick is a moment, a second, shortened to sec

explanation.surface: Someone clearing ticked boxes on a form after an unexplained message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tick' looks like a checkmark beside the 'boxes', but it is a short moment of time.
explanation.definitionFit: To exsect is a surgical term meaning to remove by cutting, to excise.

clue.text: Ready in good time once the right pair assembled

indicators.note: assembled means put together from parts, so the letters are built into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: A couple, the correct two, gathered promptly as arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks the definition as an old word, not a time clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Rathripe is an archaic word for ripening early, so mature or prepared before the usual season.

clue.text: Game business graduate makes dance

blocks.note: RU is rugby union
a Master of Business Administration

explanation.surface: A graduate's business venture in the gaming world turns into a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue invites 'game business' as one phrase, but the split is after 'Game'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom step with swaying hip movements, danced to Latin rhythms.

clue.text: Cross after brasserie emptied by gong and loud buzzer

indicators.note: an emptied word has had its contents removed, leaving only its outer letters

blocks.note: first and last letters
a gong is British slang for a medal or honour, such as the MBE
a cross is the letter X

explanation.surface: Someone cross after a restaurant empties at the dinner gong, with an alarm buzzing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross after' puts X at the end. An MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: Bembex is a genus of sand wasps, noted for the loud buzz they make in flight.

clue.text: Fur-coated creature visiting fair

blocks.note: visiting a place is being at it
fair, as in passable, is OK

explanation.surface: A furry animal spotted at a funfair.
explanation.definitionFit: The atok is a South American skunk, an animal clad in thick fur.

clue.text: Journalists brought about change in N Korea

indicators.note: to bring about is also to turn round, so the letters face the other way

blocks.note: the National Union of Journalists

explanation.surface: Reporters forced a policy shift in Pyongyang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' looks like reform, but it means small coins. The NUJ is the main British journalists' trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: The jun is a North Korean monetary unit, one hundredth of a won, so loose coins there.

clue.text: Plant in medium Yorkshire town mostly not that great ultimately

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the town name drops its last letter
ultimately points to the very end of the word before it
'in' signals that one group of letters is put inside another

blocks.note: M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium
Ilkley is a spa town in West Yorkshire
this as opposed to that
last letter

explanation.surface: A plant growing in a modest Yorkshire town that is not quite great.
explanation.walkthrough: The town loses its Y and is split after its third letter to take the 'not that' and the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk thistle is a purple-flowered Mediterranean herb with white-veined leaves, used in herbal medicine.

clue.text: Dare perhaps to enter joint after flipping frenzied females!

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so the name goes into the joint
flipping means turning over, so the result is read backwards

blocks.note: a seam is a joint between two pieces
Dan Dare, the space hero of the British comic Eagle

explanation.surface: Wild women dared to break into a marijuana cigarette after losing their heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dare perhaps' looks like a challenge, but Dare is a surname; 'perhaps' shows Dan is one way to name him. The joint is a seam, not a spliff.
explanation.definitionFit: Maenads were the raving female followers of Dionysus in Greek myth, known for ecstatic wildness.

clue.text: One knight holding sword back, trapping another in cone-shaped mesh

indicators.note: back means the word for sword is written in the opposite direction
holding means having inside, so the first knight goes round the weapon
trapping means catching and enclosing, so the weapon then encloses the second knight

blocks.note: Kt is the abbreviation for knight
an épée is a fencing sword
another knight, N in chess notation

explanation.surface: A knight with his sword drawn back, catching a rival in a net.
explanation.walkthrough: The two knights take different standard forms, one as in titles, the other as on a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepnet is a long tubular net staked in the water by anglers to hold their live catch.
